BREAKING: The head of the army says the UK's political leaders are about to start a "frank conversation" with the public about the need to prepare for war, per Sky News.

General Sir Roly Walker said every citizen will be asked to make sacrifices and to play their part in the defence of the nation.

BREAKING: Meta, Amazon, Microsoft and Google are expected to pour $750 billion into capital spending this year, mostly on AI data centers, per Bloomberg.

That’s enough to write a $5,500 check to every household in America.

It’s up more than 80% from last year’s $410 billion.

U.S. consumer confidence just fell to its lowest level since 2014, per The Conference Board.

The expectations index sits near 60, well below 80, the level The Conference Board says has historically signaled a recession ahead.

Ray Dalio is warning that America’s biggest foreign lenders are pulling back.

China and Japan, two of the largest foreign holders of U.S. Treasuries, are showing weaker demand for American debt.

China’s holdings have been cut by more than half, from $1.3 trillion in 2013 to about $618 billion.

Japan still holds about $1.1 trillion.

Less foreign buying could mean higher borrowing costs for the US.
China tells Israel to stop 'forced establishment' of West Bank settlements, per BBC

The U.S. economy hasn’t had a recession in 78 months.

That’s the 6th-longest expansion since 1854, based on NBER data, and nearly double the long-term average of about 41 months.

The all-time record is 128 months, from 2009 to 2020.

If this run lasts until early 2031, it will take the crown.
Trump: I know more about inflation, I know more about everything than anybody in this room. Anybody anywhere in the world.
